entities.summary:
Dmitry of Tver, Prince of Tver from 1318 and Grand Prince of Vladimir from 1322, played a pivotal role in shaping the medieval Russian state. He was known as the Fearsome Eyes or the Terrible Eyes, a nickname earned due to his cunning and strategic military campaigns.

Born into a noble family, Dmitry's ascension to power was marked by his ability to navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the Grand Duchy of Moscow, the Golden Horde, and the Mongol Empire. His diplomatic efforts, coupled with his military prowess, allowed him to expand Tver's borders and establish it as a major power in northeastern Russia.

Dmitry's legacy extends beyond his military conquests, as he also played a key role in the development of the Russian Orthodox Church and the establishment of the Principality of Vladimir-Suzdal. His death in 1326, executed by the Mongols in Sarai, marked the beginning of a period of turmoil and instability in the region.

The execution of Dmitry of Tver serves as a stark reminder of the brutal realities of medieval politics, where power was often won and lost through bloodshed and strategic maneuvering.
